tasks.short: Match applications to the vacancy: certificates, shift, site and CAO group.

today.trigger: A pile of new applications sits on an open vacancy in Recruitee, or a site manager asks who has applied.
steps: Open the vacancy in Recruitee and the job order on SharePoint: site, shift, CAO function group, certificates, language needed for the safety briefing.
Read each application and CV, including the same person sent by an agency and direct.
Check forklift, VCA and food-safety claims against the vacancy, and note rota and travel to Rotterdam, Tilburg or Venlo.
Mark a first yes, maybe or no, usually in Excel, for the hiring manager.
drudgery: Hunting the same certificate lines on every CV
Merging duplicate people from direct applications and the three agencies
Rebuilding the sheet when a manager changes a must-have
today.time_sinks: The hours go to reading every application the same way, including clear mismatches, and to redoing the comparison when the job order shifts.

lenses.faster: The line-by-line hunt for certificates, shift and CAO group disappears. Review of the reasons, the duplicates and every borderline file remains, about three fifths of today's hours on current volume, because that review has to be able to overturn the order.
lenses.autonomous: A new application on an open vacancy starts a comparison against the written job order only. The recruiter decides who is proposed and who is parked; a rejection is sent only after that decision.
lenses.ambitious: Night-shift team leads in Tilburg and Venlo, who rarely sit in the daytime screen, get a Monday list of people who can work their rota, including internals and flex workers with valid certificates. Site demand for that list would grow if it were cheap, because those shifts are filled late and mostly by phone.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss chasing certificate dates and duplicate agency CVs. The work they want more of is judging people whose experience does not sit neatly on the job order, with the manager who runs the shift.
lenses.options: A strict certificate cut, a cut that allows a certificate booked before day one, and an internal-across-sites cut put different people in front of the manager. The recruiter picks the cut with the manager before anyone is rejected.
lenses.altitude: The week moves to borderline files and to agreeing which lines on the job order are fixed. The recruiter gains the say on whether a requirement is a must-have or a preference for that vacancy, which is more expert work than reading PDFs.
reach: The People Analytics and HRIS Analyst's first look at which requirements show up among people still employed at day 90. The recruiter would need the Power BI HR dashboard and the limits of the nightly AFAS extract.

tasks.human_edge: The recruiter knows which line on a Venlo or Rotterdam job order is real for that dock and which was copied from the last vacancy, and when a missing VCA can be booked before day one.
tasks.pattern_why: The comparison can be drafted from the job order, but the recruiter has to be free to overturn it. A rejection that only follows a score is not allowed, and the works council has to agree before this comparison runs.

in_practice.trigger: A new application arrives in Recruitee for an open vacancy, or the recruiter opens the pile.
steps: Load the vacancy's signed requirements: certificates, CAO function group, site, shift, language for the safety briefing.
Merge duplicates across direct applications and agency submissions.
Draft a row per person: met, missing or unclear, each with a reason taken only from the application and documents they supplied.
The recruiter opens every borderline file and a sample of the rest, corrects bad reasons, and sets propose or park.
Record the criteria version and every change of order on the vacancy.
in_practice.human_gate: The recruiter decides who is proposed to the manager and who is parked. The park list becomes a rejection only when the recruiter confirms it.
data_needed: Signed must-haves and preferences
The application and its attachments
Certificate claims the person supplied
Site, shift and CAO function group
Whether the person is internal, direct or via an agency
in_practice.logs_to: The Recruitee timeline, plus a criteria-version note on the vacancy that the OR and a later auditor can read.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit 8 can build a profile from an application and calculate a match score against open vacancies; the description gives no accuracy figure.
The Dutch DPA says recruitment decisions may not rest solely on a score, and there is no meaningful human intervention if the assessor must follow the outcome.
CV screening almost always needs prior works-council consent under WOR art. 27(1)(k) and (l), and nullity can be invoked within one month.
Of 1,000+ US hiring leaders, 67% use AI for CV screening and 26% fear they no longer see some candidates; 71% believe most applications they screen are AI-written.

risks: Turning this on before OR consent leaves the screening open to a nullity challenge within a month.
If the recruiter always follows the rank, the review is not meaningful under the AVG.
Scores built from data beyond the application are the fight in Kistler v. Eightfold; Noordhaven stays responsible for the outcome.
More AI-written applications can put the saved reading time back into a larger pile.
From 2 December 2027, filtering applications is high-risk and needs an overseer, six-month logs, and information to the OR.
research_questions: On a sample of last quarter's vacancies, what share of rejections does the recruiter reverse after reading the file behind the reason?
Has the OR already consented to application comparison, and on what conditions?
Among people who only met the certificate rules and people who ranked high, who was still employed at day 90?
How many applications per vacancy are duplicates or AI-written, and does that volume remove the time saving?

tasks.short: Explain pay, shifts, duties and conditions to people who applied.

today.trigger: A candidate asks about pay, hours or the work, or reaches the stage where Noordhaven sends the vacancy pack.
steps: Look up the CAO scale, shift allowances, roster and site conditions in SharePoint or an old mail.
Check certificates the role needs before day one, such as VCA, forklift or food safety.
Write or reuse an Outlook mail, in Dutch or English, and talk the serious candidates through it.
Answer follow-ups on nights, weekend allowances, travel and what a fixed contract would mean.
drudgery: Finding the current scale and toeslagen for the same vacancy again
Keeping the Dutch and English mails in line
Rewriting the roster because the last mail was for a different site
today.time_sinks: Most hours go to repeating standard facts, and to long back-and-forth when the first mail was vague on pay or the rota.

lenses.faster: Looking up the scale, allowances and roster for every reply disappears once the vacancy fact sheet is signed. A standard pack then takes the recruiter no time; a real question still takes the call or the mail it takes today.
lenses.autonomous: Reaching the 'share the pack' stage in Recruitee sends the approved pack for that vacancy. Anything the sheet does not cover, including a person's own flex situation, waits for the recruiter.
lenses.ambitious: Flex workers already on site get a written comparison of agency work and a direct Noordhaven contract, using figures Compensation and Benefits has signed. Demand would grow in peak season, when that choice is made often and currently by rumour.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss pasting the same scale and roster into Outlook. They want more of the conversation with someone close to yes, about the shift they will actually work.
lenses.options: A day-shift pack and a weekend-shift pack, with the allowance difference taken from the sheet, lead some candidates to continue and others to stop. The recruiter chooses the pack.
lenses.altitude: Repetitive mail leaves the week, and the remaining conversations are with people near an offer. The recruiter gains the right to publish a fact sheet that Compensation and Benefits and the site manager have signed, and gets sharper about which conditions decide acceptance.
reach: The Compensation and Benefits Specialist's first-line explanation of the CAO scale and shift allowances to candidates. The recruiter would need the current scales, the toeslagen, and a written rule for questions only Compensation and Benefits may answer.

tasks.human_edge: A person choosing between a flex contract and a fixed one needs a straight answer on the early start, the cold store, and whether the team lead is stable. The recruiter hears the hesitation and knows when to stop selling the rota.
tasks.pattern_why: Pay, allowances and rosters are known figures per vacancy. A template that can only insert signed figures will keep a scale from being invented. Questions the sheet does not cover return to the recruiter.

in_practice.trigger: A candidate reaches the pack stage in Recruitee, or asks a question that matches a heading on the signed fact sheet.
steps: Compensation and Benefits and the site manager sign the fact sheet: duties, CAO scale, allowances, roster, site conditions, certificates, promotion steps, Dutch and English.
On the stage change, send the matching pack from the company mailbox and file it on the Recruitee timeline.
If the question is not on the sheet, or is about this person's flex contract, route it to the recruiter.
The recruiter answers those, checks any figure with Compensation and Benefits, and sends the reply.
in_practice.human_gate: The recruiter, with Compensation and Benefits, signs the fact sheet before it can send. Every unanswered question and every flex-to-fixed comparison waits for the recruiter.
data_needed: The signed fact sheet and its version
The candidate's question and language
Stage in Recruitee
Whether the person is flex, internal or a direct applicant
in_practice.logs_to: The sent item in Outlook and the same text on the Recruitee timeline, with the fact-sheet version.

evidence.claim: A recruiter-reviewed email or job ad does not need an AI label; a candidate-facing chatbot does, at the first turn, including who it acts for.
Among 1,000+ US hiring leaders, 57% use AI to draft job descriptions, and about 4 in 5 say they are managing a problem with their use of AI.
CAO scales and shift allowances are a finite set of signed figures, so a mail-merge from an approved sheet can carry them without a model.

risks: A sheet signed months ago drifts from the CAO text Payroll uses in AFAS.
Dutch and English packs diverge and candidates compare them.
A flex-to-fixed comparison misstates the agency rate or cuts across the agency contract.
Candidates treat the pack as a binding offer.
research_questions: What share of these contacts last month were standard questions, and what share needed a real conversation?
How often does the pay on the accepted offer differ from the first figure the candidate was sent?
Is the scale on SharePoint the one Payroll has in AFAS for that function group?
Do the three agency contracts allow Noordhaven to discuss a direct contract with a flex worker?

tasks.short: Decide who the manager should see, and recommend who to hire.

today.trigger: Enough reviewed applicants sit on a vacancy, or a manager asks for a shortlist or a hire recommendation.
steps: Re-read the must-haves with the manager and pull the people marked propose.
Collect certificates, availability, site and the interview notes already in Recruitee.
Talk the manager through the names, often on Teams between shifts.
Write a recommendation when they are ready to hire, hold or stop.
drudgery: Reformatting Recruitee notes into a mail the manager will actually read
Chasing interview feedback that was never entered
Rebuilding the pack because one must-have changed
today.time_sinks: The hours sit in assembling the pack and in waiting for a manager who is on shift, more than in the hiring judgment itself.

lenses.faster: Building the comparison pack drops from a couple of hours to a read-through of a draft table. The conversation with the manager and the recommendation the recruiter writes take about as long as they do now.
lenses.autonomous: When a vacancy has a reviewed pile, a comparison table is drafted on the agreed criteria. The recruiter writes the recommendation, and names go to the manager only after that.
lenses.ambitious: A documented keep-or-release recommendation for a flex worker the site wants on a fixed contract, on the same criteria as an external hire, would be made every time a peak ends. Demand would grow if it were cheap, because those choices are now corridor conversations with no file.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss reformatting feedback into an email. They want the argument about who will still be productive at day 90, and the room to send back a thin 'I like this one'.
lenses.options: One table ordered by ready-to-start and one ordered by closeness to a team-lead path put different people in the interview slots. The manager sees both before anyone is invited.
lenses.altitude: More of the week is the recommendation and less is assembling packs. The recruiter gains the right to withhold a name that fails an agreed must-have, and to put an internal or flex person on the same page as an external one. The job becomes more expert.
reach: The HR Business Partner's first structuring of hiring criteria with the site manager. The recruiter would need to read that department's leaver pattern on the Power BI board, and to keep a person's absence record out of the selection file.

tasks.human_edge: The recruiter has hired for this team lead before and knows who will clash with a small crew, and which quiet internal candidate the manager underrates. The table has the file; the recruiter has the team.
tasks.pattern_why: The table can be drafted. The recommendation is the hiring decision, so the recruiter writes it and can ignore the order. Privacy rules require that freedom to be real, and interview notes stay the interviewer's own words.

in_practice.trigger: The recruiter marks a vacancy ready for shortlist, after the match review.
steps: Draft a comparison on the agreed criteria, certificates, site, shift and the notes already typed in Recruitee.
Quote those notes. Leave interview text as the interviewer wrote it.
The recruiter reorders, drops and adds names, and writes the recommendation in their own words.
Send the pack to the hiring manager, including the night-shift supervisor when they are the decision maker.
Record the decision and the reasons on the Recruitee timeline.
in_practice.human_gate: The recruiter confirms every name before it goes to a manager, and writes the hire recommendation. A rank does not hire, reject or invite.
data_needed: Agreed criteria and the criteria version
Applications and certificate status
Interview notes the interviewer wrote
Shift availability and site
Manager and, where relevant, the night-shift supervisor
in_practice.logs_to: The Recruitee timeline: names sent, names withheld, the recommendation text, and the manager's decision.

evidence.claim: There is no meaningful human intervention if the person assessing applications must follow the automated outcome.
AI interview summaries become the record managers read; notetakers err, drop context and can store an unlawful question.
Liability for hiring AI stays with the employer. Mobley v. Workday continues on disparate impact, and a vendor contract does not decide whether a statute applies.
From 2 December 2027, evaluating candidates is a high-risk use. Deployers then need a competent overseer, logs kept six months, and must inform workers' representatives.

risks: Managers treat the table order as the decision and stop reading the people.
A generated interview summary replaces the interview and can keep a forbidden question.
Criteria such as years in a Dutch warehouse or full availability can narrow who gets through without a job reason.
Flex and internal people never appear if the pack only reads external Recruitee applications.
The OR has not agreed the shortlist method.
research_questions: Last quarter, how often did the manager hire the person at the top of the recruiter's list, and who was still here at day 90?
Which must-haves did managers override, and what happened to those hires at day 90?
Are flex workers and internal movers in the file at the moment of shortlist?
What would the OR require before a ranked shortlist is shown to managers?

tasks.short: Tell applicants where their application stands.

today.trigger: A stage changes, a candidate asks for news, or someone has been waiting with no message.
steps: Check the Recruitee stage and whether the manager has actually decided.
Choose a mail or a call, and Dutch or English.
Write the status, often in a batch on Friday.
Answer the replies and the chases.
drudgery: The Friday rejection batch
Retyping 'still in review' because a manager has not decided
Searching the timeline to see what the candidate was last told
today.time_sinks: The hours go to delayed, repeated status mail, and to candidates who chase because nothing was sent.

lenses.faster: Writing the standard received, in-review and rejection mails disappears; they go when the stage changes. The call list and the replies remain, about a third of the hours this task takes now.
lenses.autonomous: A Recruitee stage change sends the matching approved template, and a stage past its agreed days flags the recruiter with the manager's name. Rejection and offer stages exist only after the recruiter has decided.
lenses.ambitious: A near-miss with a still-valid certificate can be told about one named vacancy at another site, when the recruiter has turned that on for the vacancy family. The three sites would use it if it were cheap, because each now restarts the search from empty.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss the rejection batch. They want a clean record that people were told on time, and their hours on the candidates they are still hiring.
lenses.options: For a near miss the recruiter chooses among three ready texts: closed, kept on file for the agreed period, or pointed at one named open vacancy. That choice decides whether the person is gone or still in play.
lenses.altitude: Status becomes a rule set: which stage sends which text, in which language, and who must be called. The recruiter gains the right to set those rules per vacancy type and to see which managers are blocking a decision. The expertise shifts to candidate trust and away from mailbox volume.
reach: The HR Administrator's chasing of managers who have not recorded an outcome, which is what blocks a status. The recruiter would need the list of who is allowed to reject, and the AFAS practice for internal candidates.

tasks.human_edge: An internal warehouse worker who did not get the team-lead role needs to hear it from a person, in words that do not humiliate them on the floor the next day. A template cannot judge that moment.
tasks.pattern_why: The words for each stage can be written down, so a template tied to the Recruitee stage does the job. A model is the wrong tool for a message that must be the same every time.

in_practice.trigger: A Recruitee stage changes, or a stage is older than the days agreed for that vacancy.
steps: Map the stage to the approved Dutch or English template and fill only the candidate's name, the vacancy and the site.
Hold anyone on the stop-list: internal employee, flex worker the site knows, open complaint, or a recruiter flag to call first.
Send the template from the company mailbox and stamp the Recruitee timeline.
If the delay is a manager who has not decided, notify the recruiter with the count, the stage and the manager.
The recruiter handles the stop-list and any reply that asks for a real answer.
in_practice.human_gate: The recruiter is the only person who can move a candidate to rejected or offer. The stop-list is always a person, before any mail.
data_needed: Current stage and days in stage
Template version and language
Stop-list flags
The manager responsible for the open decision
in_practice.logs_to: The Recruitee timeline: template version, send time, and any stop-list reason.

evidence.claim: Uniper's hiring agent, given process context, flagged overdue recruiter and manager tasks and coordinated candidate emails. CIO.de reports time to contract signature fell 27 days and screening 13 days; no baseline was published.
Recruiter-reviewed emails need no AI label. A chatbot that told a candidate their status would have to say it is AI, and for whom, at the first turn.
Once a rejection is a recruiter decision stored as a stage, sending the matching template is ordinary ATS configuration and does not need a model.

risks: A wrong stage sends a rejection to someone still in process.
An internal candidate learns bad news by mail before their manager has spoken to them.
Templates go stale when a vacancy is paused or rewritten.
A cross-site suggestion is a new selection step and needs the same consent as screening.
If replies are unread, the saving comes back as a second inbox.
research_questions: How many status contacts last month were alike enough for one template per stage?
How many days do candidates sit in each Recruitee stage, and which delays are a manager who has not decided?
What share must be a call because they are internal, flex, or already known on the floor?
Is stage data clean enough that a template last month would have sent the right words?

tasks.short: Look for people who could do the open jobs, inside and outside.

today.trigger: A vacancy is approved, a role passes its target fill date, or a site asks for names the advert has not produced.
steps: Search Recruitee for earlier candidates, then boards, referrals and the three agency portals.
Ask team leads who on the floor wants a move, and check Studytube only when someone remembers.
Write to the people worth contacting, by mail or LinkedIn, and log the source badly or not at all.
Brief the agency, or book a job fair, when the list is thin.
drudgery: Re-filtering last year's applicants by hand
Copying profiles into a spreadsheet
Asking all three agencies the same question in three portals
today.time_sinks: The hours go to tab-hopping across sources that do not share a key, and to outreach the recruiter half-remembers sending.

lenses.faster: Hand-searching old Recruitee piles, boards and spreadsheets disappears. Choosing who may be contacted and approving each message remain, together with job fairs and referrals, about two thirds of this task.
lenses.autonomous: An approved vacancy with a source plan, or a role past its fill target on the Power BI board, starts a search across the sources named in that plan. No message and no internal approach happens until the recruiter approves the person and the text.
lenses.ambitious: People already on the three sites — staff whose Studytube certificates match, and flex workers who have asked about a fixed contract — would be searched before any paid advert. Site managers would ask for that first if it were cheap, because they pay agency margin for people already on the floor.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss copying profiles into Excel. They want the conversation with someone who might move, and a clear view of which source is worth paying.
lenses.options: Internals first, earlier applicants first, or the agency bench first changes who is phoned this week and therefore who can be hired. The recruiter sees the three mixes before anyone is contacted.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts from hunting to setting the source mix and approving contact. The recruiter gains the right to hold a paid advert when the internal and earlier-applicant lists are deep enough. The expertise is where 90-day hires actually come from.
reach: The HR Business Partner's ad hoc list of who on a warehouse team could move. The recruiter would need contract type and certificate expiry in AFAS and Studytube, and OR agreement before employees are ranked for a vacancy.

tasks.human_edge: A name becomes a candidate when someone they trust asks them. Referrals, job-fair conversations and a team lead's 'ask her, she wants off nights' do not come from a search.
tasks.pattern_why: The useful source and the next gap change as the search proceeds, across portals that do not match. Contact still changes a person's expectations, so the recruiter approves every send and every internal approach.

in_practice.trigger: A vacancy is approved with a source plan, or it passes the fill-date mark on the dashboard.
steps: Read the source order: internal certificates, earlier Recruitee candidates, referrals, the named agencies, then external boards.
Build a list with the requirement each person meets, the gap, and the source.
Drop people already in process or already in that function.
Draft one outreach text per external person, in Dutch or English, for the recruiter to edit.
The recruiter sends, or asks the team lead to speak to an internal colleague in person, and records the source.
in_practice.human_gate: The recruiter approves each external message before it is sent. An employee is approached by a person.
data_needed: The source plan and the signed requirements
Earlier applications and their outcomes
Certificate and contract fields for internals
What each agency contract allows
Referral names the site actually supplied
in_practice.logs_to: The Recruitee source field and timeline, so a later day-90 check can see where the person came from.

evidence.claim: Workday's Talent Acquisition Agent flags roles at risk of missing their fill date and drafts outreach. Outreach still needs recruiter approval, and customers set which actions run alone. General availability is early 2027.
A sourcing agent that contacts a candidate itself must say it is AI, and for whom, at the first turn. Fines run up to €15 million or 3% of turnover.
Kistler v. Eightfold attacks match scores built from data beyond the application, and the employer remains responsible.
Staff-selection tooling almost always needs prior works-council consent under WOR art. 27.

risks: Searching AFAS and Studytube to rank employees is a selection system and needs OR consent first.
Agency contracts may forbid using portal data to recruit those workers direct.
A long list of approved messages still costs the recruiter the hour the search just saved.
From 2 December 2027, targeting of job ads is high-risk.
Silver-medalist pools kept without a retention rule and consent conflict with the AVG.
research_questions: Which source produced the hires still here at day 90 over the last four quarters, and is that source stored in Recruitee?
Do AFAS and Studytube hold a usable internal list: certificate, expiry, contract, site and shift?
What do the three agency contracts allow when Noordhaven offers a flex worker a direct job?
Would the OR treat a search for 'who could be a team lead' as a selection method that needs prior consent?

tasks.short: Check that our selection criteria are still fair and useful.

today.trigger: A site wants a new hurdle, a hire fails badly, or someone asks whether the criteria still make sense. It happens less often than the pile of CVs.
steps: Export Recruitee stages to Excel and try to match them to AFAS start dates.
Ask Payroll or the HRBP for day-90 still-in-seat, and sometimes early exits.
Look at pass rates by site with numbers that are usually small.
Recommend, in a mail or a meeting, that a criterion stay or change.
drudgery: Rebuilding the same export because Recruitee and AFAS do not share a key
Arguing from memory which hurdle is a habit
Formatting a note the OR can read
today.time_sinks: The hours go to assembling data that does not join, so the recommendation is late or never written.

lenses.faster: Pulling stage drop-off and day-90 outcomes out of exports shrinks when an extract exists. Checking small numbers and writing the recommendation still take the meeting they take now, and that remains most of the task.
lenses.autonomous: Each quarter, and whenever a site adds a must-have, a draft note is prepared from the agreed criteria and the outcome extract. No job order changes until the recruiter and the HRBP accept the revision.
lenses.ambitious: Every new hurdle a site wants — extra years, Dutch-only, an extra certificate — would get an outcome note before it is used, not only after a complaint. Demand for that decision would grow if it were cheap, because hurdles are added whenever a hire fails and today they stick.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss rebuilding Excel from Recruitee. They want the argument about which hurdle is real, in a note the OR can read.
lenses.options: The same hurdle shown for all hires, by site, and for flex-to-fixed only can stay in one cut and go in another. The recruiter brings those cuts to the HRBP before the job order is rewritten.
lenses.altitude: The month includes a criteria review with the HRBP, not a scramble before an audit. The recruiter gains the right to hold a new must-have that has no job reason and no outcome behind it, pending the HR Director and the OR where the method changes. That is more expert work.
reach: The People Analytics and HRIS Analyst's funnel and outcome tables, which appear when the HR Director asks. The recruiter would need small-number caution and the limits of the nightly AFAS extract.

tasks.human_edge: A gap in pass rates is not a reason to drop a forklift certificate the insurer or the law requires. The recruiter, with the site and Compensation and Benefits, knows which criteria are obligations and which are habit.
tasks.pattern_why: The tables can be drafted. The recommendation changes who can be hired and can be a change of selection method, so the recruiter stays responsible for the advice and the OR path stays open.

in_practice.trigger: The quarter turns, or a manager asks to add or drop a must-have.
steps: List the current criteria and mark each as legal or insurer requirement, CAO requirement, or local habit.
Attach aggregate outcomes only: stage drop-off, still employed at day 90, and first-month exit, by vacancy family and site.
Draft what the numbers can and cannot support, with the sample size beside each cut.
The recruiter and the HRBP agree keep, change or park, and the recruiter writes the recommendation.
File the note. Where the selection method changes, send it through the HR Director to the OR before the job order changes.
in_practice.human_gate: The recruiter and the HRBP decide the recommendation. A criterion changes only after the path they set, including the OR where WOR art. 27 applies.
data_needed: The criteria list and why each line exists
A join from Recruitee candidate to AFAS employee and start date
Aggregate day-90 employment and aggregate early exit
Sample size per site and vacancy family
in_practice.logs_to: A quarterly criteria note on the HR SharePoint, with the extract date, the sample sizes and the recommendation, readable by the OR.

evidence.claim: The Dutch DPA's AI impact barometer finds recruitment AI weak on explainability and calls for action.
Workday's own TA team generated interview questions for 800+ skills across 1,600+ roles, with no evidence that hires improved.
A dismissed US claim, Harper v. Sirius XM, shows the plaintiff could not prove the mechanism, not that the tool was fair.
From 2 December 2027, filtering applications and evaluating candidates are high-risk, and deployers must inform workers' representatives.

risks: Site-level numbers are small and look like a pattern.
Day-90 exit mixes a weak hire with a bad rota, so a criterion is blamed for the shift pattern.
A draft recommends dropping a certificate the insurer or the arbodienst requires.
Changing the selection method without OR consent is open to challenge.
Past hires are only the people who were allowed in. Individual verzuim is special-category data and does not belong in this note.
research_questions: Can Recruitee stages be joined to AFAS start dates and still-employed-at-day-90 without a manual Excel, and how many hires a year does that cover?
Which current must-haves are required by law, insurer or CAO, and which are local habit?
What sample size per site would the HRBP need before they changed a hurdle?
What would the OR require in a quarterly criteria note before they would use it?

tasks.short: Set the plan for how each site fills its seats this season.

today.trigger: Budget season, a peak warning from a site, or a vacancy list that no longer matches who is actually leaving.
steps: Ask the three sites and the HRBPs what they expect to need, often by mail and Teams.
Pull open roles from Recruitee and last month's agency hours from three portals.
Look at the Power BI board for headcount and agency cost, which Finance also has.
Write a short plan: direct hire, flex, or both, and take it to the HR Director.
drudgery: Chasing three agency portals for hours that do not match Finance
Rewriting a yearly plan that was stale by March
Copying the same vacancy list into another slide
today.time_sinks: The hours go to assembling a picture each source already holds in part, so the strategy meeting starts with arguing about the numbers.

lenses.faster: Collecting last peak's hires, open roles and agency hours into one note shrinks to checking a draft. The meeting with the HR Director and the site managers stays the length it is now.
lenses.autonomous: A monthly date, or a site warning that orders are up, starts a draft with three source mixes from the pipeline and the agency figures. Nothing is posted and no agency is briefed until the recruiter and the HRBP agree the mix.
lenses.ambitious: A monthly per-site choice of direct hire, flex, and flex-to-fixed, made before peak and whenever a site is short, would replace the yearly habit plus a panic call. Site managers would ask for it if it were cheap, because they currently call an agency first.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss chasing portal numbers. They want the argument about where a permanent contract is worth it, and a plan they can defend to the HR Director.
lenses.options: Direct-hire heavy, flex heavy, and convert-flex-workers-who-hold-the-certificates are three plans that open different vacancies and brief the agencies differently. The meeting picks one.
lenses.altitude: The week includes a source-mix proposal per site instead of one annual plan. The recruiter gains the right to put that proposal, with last year's 90-day results, in front of the HR Director. The work becomes more expert: how Noordhaven staffs a peak, not how a requisition gets filled.
reach: The FP&A Analyst's first translation of warehouse volume into hours and heads. The recruiter would need to see how the Controller counts agency cost against payroll, and to leave the budget decision with Finance and the HR Director.

tasks.human_edge: A scenario does not know that Rotterdam's team leads are tired of training people who leave in week three, or that Tilburg's OR members will challenge a swing to more fixed contracts. The recruiter hears that in the room and changes the plan.
tasks.pattern_why: The mixes can be drafted from pipeline and cost figures. Choosing how a site staffs is a management decision the recruiter prepares and the HR Director takes, so the person stays the lead.

in_practice.trigger: The monthly staffing cycle, or a written site warning that volume or absence will open seats.
steps: Pull open vacancies, days open, hires still here at day 90, and agency hours and cost by site.
Draft three mixes for the next period: direct, flex, and flex-to-fixed, each with the seats and the sites.
The recruiter checks the figures with the HRBP and marks what Finance has not confirmed.
The HR Director and the site managers choose the mix.
Only then does the recruiter open vacancies, brief an agency, or stop a search.
in_practice.human_gate: The HR Director, with the site, chooses the mix. The recruiter does not brief an agency or open a campaign on the draft alone.
data_needed: Open vacancies and days open
Day-90 employment of recent hires by source and site
Agency hours and cost Finance will stand behind
A site volume or leaver note, when one exists
in_practice.logs_to: The monthly staffing note on SharePoint, next to the mix the HR Director agreed.

evidence.claim: Workday's Talent Acquisition Agent flags roles at risk of missing their fill date. Early adopters have it now; general availability is early 2027.
Uniper's agent was useful on process context, such as candidates sitting on a shortlist more than 14 days, and gave only generalities on raw HR data.
A ManpowerGroup result cited by HR Dive: under 5% of employers saw transformational results from AI in hiring.

risks: Agency hours in the portals do not match AFAS or the Controller, so the meeting argues the extract.
A monthly mix cuts past the HRBP and the site, and the recruiter does not hold the labour budget.
Rewarding speed to fill works against a hire who is still productive at day 90.
Peak forecasts from operations arrive late or stay verbal.
research_questions: Is there one monthly figure for agency hours, agency cost and direct hires per site that Finance and HR both trust?
How far ahead do sites know peak volume, and is that forecast written down where HR can read it?
Did last year's direct hires and flex conversions differ on day-90 employment?
Who may change the agency-versus-direct mix today: the HR Director, the site, or both?

tasks.short: Design, run and review the tests we give applicants.

today.trigger: A role family has no agreed way to see the work, or a manager no longer trusts the interview. This is occasional, not weekly.
steps: Invent or reuse questions or a short practical trial with the team lead.
Run it on site or in a Teams call, with the recruiter or the team lead scoring.
Add up a paper sheet and put a note in Recruitee.
Rarely check whether the people who passed were still here and useful at day 90.
drudgery: Retotalling paper score sheets
Reusing vague culture-fit questions
Discovering late that the test repeats a VCA or forklift certificate Studytube already tracks
today.time_sinks: The hours go to improvising the exercise and to travelling or calling so it can be sat, not to learning whether it predicts a good 90 days.

lenses.faster: A first draft of a practical exercise and the adding-up of a checklist no longer start from a blank page. Sitting the exercise with the candidate, or briefing the team lead who sits it, takes about as long as it does now.
lenses.autonomous: When a role family has no agreed exercise, or an item's results look unrelated to day-90 retention, a draft exercise and an item review are prepared from the job tasks. No candidate sits it until the recruiter and the site manager accept it, and the OR path is done where the method changes.
lenses.ambitious: Experienced order pickers and drivers who interview badly, including flex workers, would get a practical work-sample in plain Dutch on the site, including on the night shift. Sites would use it for volume roles if a team lead could run it without the recruiter travelling, which they will not do while it is scarce.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss adding up paper sheets and arguing about a vague fit question. They want an exercise the team lead respects because it looks like the job, and a clean reason to drop an item.
lenses.options: A short practical trial, a plain-language safety-briefing check, or both, change who passes, especially among people with dock experience and weaker Dutch. The recruiter sees a pilot of both before either becomes the rule.
lenses.altitude: Less of the month is a blank page, more is deciding which roles justify a test and which items still match the work. The recruiter gains the right to retire an item that does not relate to a safe, productive 90 days, with the HRBP and the OR when the method changes. The job becomes more expert about test quality.
reach: The Learning and Development Specialist's check that a test repeats a VCA, forklift or food-safety certificate. The recruiter would need to know which certificates must be valid before day one and which Studytube can schedule in week one.

tasks.human_edge: Someone on the floor has to see unsafe behaviour and stop the exercise. A score sheet also cannot hear a candidate explain a near-miss in a way that shows judgment. The recruiter decides whether Noordhaven should ask the question at all.
tasks.pattern_why: A draft exercise and a tally are useful. Giving the test, scoring a person, and keeping or dropping it change who gets hired, so the recruiter and the site stay the lead, with the works council when the method changes.

in_practice.trigger: A role family has no agreed exercise, or the quarterly criteria note flags an item.
steps: Draft a practical exercise from the real tasks, with observable checklist items and a plain-Dutch version.
Mark items already covered by a Studytube certificate, and remove personality and emotion scoring.
The recruiter and the site manager edit the draft, set adjustments for candidates who need them, and agree who may administer it.
A person on the floor runs the exercise. The checklist total is arithmetic; the recruiter confirms the result and can override it.
Compare aggregate pass results with day-90 employment before the exercise is used on the next vacancy family.
in_practice.human_gate: No candidate sits a new or changed test until the recruiter and the site manager accept it, and the OR has agreed where the selection method changes. The recruiter can override a score.
data_needed: The job tasks and the signed requirements
Certificates Studytube already records
Who may administer on which site and shift
Aggregate outcomes for people who already sat a trial, if any exist
in_practice.logs_to: The blank exercise and the completed sheets in a restricted SharePoint library, linked from the Recruitee timeline, kept with the application file.

evidence.claim: The Dutch DPA's rules on online and game-based assessments require a real human decision and restrict sole automated rejection.
Emotion inference in hiring is banned under Article 5(1)(f) of the EU AI Act.
Generating assessment content at scale, as Workday did for 800+ skills, is documented; a link to better hires is not.
A change to staff selection almost always needs prior works-council consent.

risks: A language check presented as safety becomes a Dutch filter beyond what the job needs.
A physical trial screens out disabled applicants; the duty to adjust sits with Noordhaven.
Team leads administer it differently, so scores cannot be compared across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo.
The OR withholds consent, or a test already in use has never had it.
Auto-scoring that the recruiter cannot overturn is an Art. 22 problem.
research_questions: Which roles already use a test or a trial shift, who scores it, and where are the forms?
Do any current trial results relate to day-90 employment or to first-month incidents, in data that exists?
Which hurdles are already covered by VCA, forklift or food-safety certificates in Studytube?
What has the OR already agreed about trials, tests or assessment vendors?

role.altitude: The recruiter becomes the person who runs hire-to-productive for Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo: the monthly mix of direct hire, flex and internal moves, the must-haves a site may use, and the open roles that will miss a hire still productive at day 90. Status mail, vacancy fact sheets and first-pass search lists follow from those decisions.
reach: Compensation and Benefits: first-line explanation of CAO scales and shift allowances to candidates, once the sheet is signed.
People Analytics and HRIS: the first funnel and day-90 cut by criterion and source, within what the AFAS extract can support.
HR Business Partner: the first hiring-criteria conversation with a site manager, and the first internal-mobility list after OR agreement.
HR Administrator: chasing managers whose missing decision blocks a candidate status.
Learning and Development: knowing which certificate is a pre-start must and which Studytube can schedule in week one.
FP&A: reading a volume forecast as hours and heads, while Finance and the HR Director keep the budget.
role.ceiling_note: Two recruiters, and these tasks are about 1,100 hours of each person's year, roughly seven tenths of the role. Status templates compress; selection conversations, offer talks, OR and fairness questions, job fairs and on-site tests do not. Peak season, when flex moves toward 300, fills the exception queue. The CAO texts, agency contracts, payroll, the labour budget and the Wet verbetering poortwachter track sit with Compensation and Benefits, Finance, the HR business partners and the managers. From 2 December 2027 the high-risk duties — a named overseer, six-month logs, informing the OR — add time that does not shrink when vacancies do.
skills_to_grow: Reading the Power BI HR dashboard and challenging a bad join to the nightly AFAS extract.
The transport CAO and the warehouse CAO scales and toeslagen, to the level Compensation and Benefits will let them state.
WOR art. 27 consent and what a real AVG review looks like when a score is on the table.
When a site cut is too small to act on.
What the three agency contracts allow on a direct hire of a flex worker.
role.ambitious_version: The two recruiters would fill seats from people Noordhaven already knows first: internals, earlier near-misses, and flex workers who want a contract. They would be judged on the share of open roles whose hire is still productive at day 90, by site and shift, with the criteria visible to the OR and the HR Director. CVs opened would not be the measure.
